label: High-distress heavy social-media user
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively higher loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, alongside heavier daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate education or above, and more than 5 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Uses social media heavily on a daily basis
tone: Vulnerable, distressed, and highly digitally engaged

label: Low-distress light social-media user
summary: This profile reflects respondents with comparatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and very low anxiety symptoms, alongside lighter daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Typically male, educated to graduate level or above, and reporting about 1–3 hours of social-media use per day.
behavior_markers: Reports relatively low loneliness on the UCLA-8 measure.
Shows low depressive symptom levels on the PHQ-9.
Shows very low anxiety symptom levels on the GAD-7.
Uses social media for a lighter amount of time daily compared with heavier-use groups, averaging roughly 1–3 hours per day.
tone: Stable, low-distress, and moderate in digital engagement.

label: Socially Connected Online but Emotionally Lonely
summary: This profile describes respondents who report comparatively higher loneliness while showing comparatively lower depressive and anxiety symptoms, alongside heavier daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Typically represented by a female respondent with graduate-level education or higher who uses social media about 3-5 hours per day.
behavior_markers: Reports higher average loneliness than other measured distress indicators
Spends relatively heavy amounts of time on social media each day
Online engagement may coexist with a subjective sense of social disconnection
tone: Digitally engaged, emotionally isolated, but not marked by high general depression or anxiety.

label: Low-distress light social-media user
summary: Reports comparatively low loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, alongside relatively light daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Male respondent with graduate-level education or higher who typically uses social media about 1-3 hours per day.
behavior_markers: Uses social media for a relatively limited amount of time each day
Shows low average depressive symptom scores
Shows low average anxiety symptom scores
Fits a lower-distress respondent pattern overall
